I'm very glad you and your wife found the breast cancer before it was too late. Unfortunately, that's not true for everyone. Major Richard Star, a combat-wounded Green Beret with both Bronze Stars, discovered his terminal Stage IV lung cancer—from burn pit exposure during his 25 years of service—far too late. He died in 2021 while Congress, INCLUDING YOU, continued denying him his full earned retirement.

Senator Wicker, you VOTED AGAINST the Major Richard Star Act multiple times while combat-wounded veterans like Major Star lost $1 of their military retirement for every $1 of VA disability compensation they received. This wasn't some bureaucratic oversight—this was a DELIBERATE CHOICE by Congress to financially punish our most severely wounded warriors.

Major Star spent his final days fighting for legislation that would restore concurrent receipt to medically retired veterans. He didn't live to see it pass because senators like you prioritized other spending over keeping America's promise to those who sacrificed their bodies in service.

Your wife's story shows that early detection and treatment save lives. Major Star's story shows that Congress's refusal to fully compensate combat-wounded veterans is a NATIONAL DISGRACE.

Support the Major Richard Star Act. Stop making wounded warriors choose between their earned retirement and their disability compensation.

#MajorRichardStarAct #CombatVeterans #BurnPits #KeepThePromise #VeteransDeserveMore

Senator Roger Wicker (R-MS), a retired U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel, is facing sharp scrutiny from veterans’ groups after blocking the Major Richard Star Act on October 9, 2025 — a bill he once co-sponsored and publicly supported.

The legislation would have ended the long-criticized “VA offset,” granting 54,000 medically retired, combat-injured veterans the right to receive both their earned retirement pay and VA disability compensation.

Wicker previously praised the measure in 2021, calling for its passage “as soon as possible,” but reversed course four years later, labeling it a “double benefit” the nation “cannot afford.” His action stands in direct contrast to his 2003 vote for Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP) — a nearly identical benefit expansion for 20-year retirees that he personally qualified for.

Critics now accuse Wicker of hypocrisy and misplaced priorities, pointing to his defense-industry campaign donors and support for a $1.1 trillion defense budget while denying life-changing relief to the nation’s most wounded combat veterans.
🎖️ SUMMARY
Senator Roger Wicker (R-MS), a retired U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel, once publicly co-sponsored and endorsed the Major Richard Star Act, which sought to restore full concurrent benefits for medically retired, combat-injured veterans.

💥 On October 9 2025, as Chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Wicker blocked the same bill, calling it a “double benefit” the nation “cannot afford.”

⚖️ This reversal conflicts with his own record and past advocacy for veterans — especially his 2003 vote for CRDP, which granted similar dual benefits to career retirees, including himself.
